description: Notification from NRF to subscribed NF Service Consumers for registration, deregistration, profile change, and related subscription-condition changes, including same-PLMN, different-PLMN, and intermediate-NRF delivery.

constraints.statement: The NRF shall send a POST request to each callback URI of the subscribed NF Instances.
evidence: "The operation is invoked by issuing a POST request to each callback URI of the different subscribed NF Instances."
"The NRF shall send a POST request to the callback URI."
constraints.why_interesting: This defines the required HTTP method and target for the notification API.

constraints.statement: For notifications of newly registered NF Instances, the request body shall include the nfInstanceURI of the NF Instance, an indication of the event being notified as "registration", and the new profile data.
evidence: "For notifications of newly registered NF Instances, the request body shall include ... the nfInstanceURI of the NF Instance, an indication of the event being notified ("registration"), and the new profile data"
constraints.why_interesting: This is a concrete payload requirement that can be validated in API tests.

constraints.statement: For notifications of profile changes, the request body shall include the NFInstanceID of the NF Instance whose profile changed, an indication of the event being notified as "profile change", and the new profile data.
evidence: "For notifications of changes of the profile of a NF Instance, the request body shall include the NFInstanceID ... an indication of the event being notified ("profile change"), and the new profile data."
constraints.why_interesting: This specifies the mandatory fields for a profile-change notification.

constraints.statement: For notifications of deregistration, the request body shall include the NFInstanceID of the deregistered NF Instance and an indication of the event being notified as "deregistration".
evidence: "For notifications of deregistration of the NF Instance from NRF, the request body shall include the NFInstanceID ... and an indication of the event being notified ("deregistration")."
constraints.why_interesting: This specifies the mandatory fields for a deregistration notification.

constraints.statement: When an NF Instance changes its NFStatus, the NRF shall notify subscribing entities with event type "NF_PROFILE_CHANGED", except when the new NFStatus is "CANARY_RELEASE" and the subscriber does not support the "Canary-Release" feature.
evidence: "When the NF Instance changes its NFStatus, the NRF notifies subscribing entities with an "NF_PROFILE_CHANGED" event, except if the new NFStatus changes to "CANARY_RELEASE" and the subscribing entity does not support the "Canary-Release" feature..."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a state-transition rule with an explicit exception that affects observable notification content.

constraints.statement: When an NF Instance newly registers with status "CANARY_RELEASE" and the subscribing entity does not support the "Canary-Release" feature, the NRF shall not send an "NF_REGISTERED" event to that subscribing entity.
evidence: "When an NF Instance is newly registered in NRF, the NRF notifies subscribing entities with an "NF_REGISTERED" event, except if such NF instance newly registers with status "CANARY_RELEASE" and the subscribing entity does not support the "Canary-Release" feature; in such case, the NRF does not send an "NF_REGISTERED" event to the subscribing entity."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a forbidden-notification rule that can be checked by observing absence of a callback event.

constraints.statement: When an NF Service Instance changes its NFServiceStatus to "CANARY_RELEASE" and the subscribing entity does not support the "Canary-Release" feature, the NRF shall send an "NF_PROFILE_CHANGED" notification that removes that NF Service Instance from the NF profile.
evidence: "When an NF Service Instance changes its NFServiceStatus to "CANARY_RELEASE", and the subscribing entity does not support the "Canary-Release" feature, the NRF sends a notification with an "NF_PROFILE_CHANGED" event that removes such NF Service Instance from the NF profile..."
constraints.why_interesting: This defines a specific notification behavior and payload effect for a status transition.

constraints.statement: When a monitored NF Instance starts or stops matching the subscription conditions, the NRF shall use the "NF_PROFILE_CHANGED" event type in the notification.
evidence: "...the NRF shall use the "NF_PROFILE_CHANGED" event type in the notification."
constraints.why_interesting: This ties subscription-condition changes to a required event type.

constraints.statement: When a monitored NF Instance starts or stops matching the subscription conditions, the NRF shall indicate that fact in the notification data by the presence of the "conditionEvent" attribute.
evidence: "In that case, the NRF indicates in the notification data whether the notification is due to the NF Instance to newly start or stop matching the subscription condition (i.e. based on the presence of the "conditionEvent" attribute of the NotificationData)."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a concrete response-body indicator that can be asserted in tests.

constraints.statement: If the NRF sends delta changes for an NF Service Instance other than adding a new NF Service Instance, and that NF Service Instance had not been previously discovered, the NF Service Consumer shall ignore those delta changes.
evidence: "If the NF Service Consumer receives "delta" changes related to an NF Service Instance (other than adding a new NF Service Instance) that had not been previously discovered, those changes shall be ignored by the NF Service Consumer..."
constraints.why_interesting: This is an explicit consumer-side processing rule for delta notifications.

constraints.statement: If the NRF sends delta changes for an NF Service Instance that had been previously discovered, or the delta changes add a new NF Service Instance, the NF Service Consumer shall apply those changes.
evidence: "...but any other "delta" changes related to NF Service Instances previously discovered or adding a new NF Service Instance shall be applied."
constraints.why_interesting: This is the complementary consumer-side processing rule for delta notifications.

constraints.statement: A change of authorization attributes shall trigger an "NF_PROFILE_CHANGED" notification only if the NF Instance starts or stops being authorized for an NF that subscribed to NF profile changes.
evidence: "Change of authorization attributes ... shall trigger a "NF_PROFILE_CHANGED" notification from NRF, if the change of the NF Profile results in that the NF Instance starts or stops being authorized to be accessed by an NF having subscribed to be notified about NF profile changes."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a conditional notification trigger based on authorization-state changes.

constraints.statement: If a change of authorization attributes does not cause the NF Instance to start or stop being authorized for a subscribing NF, the change shall not trigger a notification.
evidence: "Otherwise change of authorization attributes shall not trigger notification."
constraints.why_interesting: This forbids unnecessary notifications and is directly testable by observing callback traffic.

constraints.statement: Notifications of new registrations or updates of existing registrations shall not include the content or changes of authorization attributes unless the subscribing entity explicitly requested it via completeProfileSubscription and the NRF authorized the request.
evidence: "The notifications of new registrations, or updates of existing registrations, shall not include the content (or the changes) of the authorization attributes ... unless the subscribing entity explicitly requested so, in the "completeProfileSubscription" attribute ... and the NRF authorized such a request."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a clear response-content restriction with an explicit exception.

constraints.statement: On success, the NF Service Consumer shall return 204 No Content.
evidence: "2a. On success, "204 No content" shall be returned by the NF Service Consumer."
constraints.why_interesting: This is the required success status code for the callback response.

constraints.statement: If the NF Service Consumer does not consider the nfStatusNotificationUri a valid notification URI, it shall return 404 Not Found with ProblemDetails.
evidence: "If the NF Service Consumer does not consider the "nfStatusNotificationUri" as a valid notification URI ... the NF Service Consumer shall return "404 Not Found" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error."
constraints.why_interesting: This defines an error response and required diagnostic payload.

constraints.statement: In case of redirection, the NF Service Consumer shall return a 3xx status code containing a Location header.
evidence: "In the case of redirection, the NF service consumer shall return 3xx status code, which shall contain a Location header..."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a testable redirect requirement on the callback response.

constraints.statement: The Location header in a redirection response shall contain a URI pointing to the endpoint of another NF service consumer endpoint.
evidence: "...with a Location header with an URI pointing to the endpoint of another NF service consumer endpoint."
constraints.why_interesting: This constrains the redirect target and can be validated by inspecting the header value.

constraints.statement: For notifications in a different PLMN, the POST request shall be sent directly from the NRF in the Home PLMN to the NF Service Consumer in the Serving PLMN without involvement of the NRF in the Serving PLMN.
evidence: "the POST request shall be sent directly from the NRF in Home PLMN to the NF Service Consumer in Serving PLMN, without involvement of the NRF in Serving PLMN."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a cross-PLMN routing restriction that can be checked by architecture-level integration tests.

constraints.statement: For notifications via an intermediate NRF, the POST request shall be sent directly from NRF-2 to the NF Service Consumer without involvement of NRF-1.
evidence: "The POST request shall be sent directly from NRF-2 to the NF Service Consumer without involvement of NRF-1."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a routing restriction for the intermediate-NRF notification path.
